rounds.response: Good questions — do this: For Student A, reporting means and SDs for 5‑point Likert items is acceptable but also show medians and IQRs (or note skewness) if distributions are non‑normal or you want to respect ordinality, and state your reporting choice in the methods. For Student B, round coefficients and SEs to two decimal places (three if values are very small), report CIs to two decimals, give p‑values to three decimals (use p < 0.001 for tiny values), and report effect sizes to two decimals; standardizing continuous predictors is fine—do so for interpretability but note that you standardized and, if helpful, translate at least one key coefficient back to original units.
